They provide a set amount of income support, not full wage replacement.

Can you receive both workers' compensation and EI sickness benefits?Yes, if you're eligible for both. How do I apply for EI sickness benefits?You can apply online through the Service Canada website or by phone. You'll need to provide personal and employment details, as well as information about your medical condition. You should apply as soon as possible after becoming unable to work, as there may be a waiting period before benefits start.

What happens if my EI sickness benefits are denied?If your application for EI sickness benefits is denied, you have the right to appeal the decision. You can request a reconsideration of the decision within 30 days of receiving the denial letter. The appeal process may involve providing additional medical information or clarifying your employment history.

Can I work part-time while receiving EI sickness benefits?If you're receiving EI sickness benefits, you may be able to work part-time and still receive partial benefits. However, if you earn more than a certain amount (called the "earnings exemption"), your benefits may be reduced. It's important to report any earnings to Service Canada so they can adjust your benefits if necessary.

What happens to my EI benefits if I go back to work before the expected end date?If you return to work before the expected end date of your EI sickness benefits, you must report this to Service Canada. Depending on how much you earn, your benefits might stop or be adjusted. You may also be eligible for a "top-up" if your new earnings are less than your previous income and you continue to meet the eligibility criteria.

Are EI sickness benefits taxable?Yes, EI sickness benefits are considered taxable income. When you apply, you can choose to have income tax withheld from your benefits at source, or you can report the benefits as income when you file your taxes. Service Canada will provide you with a T4E slip at the end of the tax year, showing the amount of benefits you received.
